candidates.name: Chronic Urticaria
support_spans: A woman in her 50s presented with a 2.5-year history of severe urticaria.
The primary symptom was chronic pruritus, which was worsening and refractory to treatment.
candidates.why: The patient's long history of severe urticaria and chronic pruritus supports this diagnosis.

candidates.name: Dermal Hypersensitivity
support_spans: Skin biopsies: Two 0.4-mm punch biopsies revealed dermal edema with sparse chronic inflammation and dilated blood vessels within the superficial dermis, consistent with dermal hypersensitivity.
candidates.why: The skin biopsy results are consistent with dermal hypersensitivity.

candidates.name: Contact Dermatitis
support_spans: Skin patch testing showed positive results for methylisothiazolinones
candidates.why: The positive skin patch test results for methylisothiazolinones suggest contact dermatitis.
